messages:
maria: Observed a repeat of the multi-node TP runs stalling during warmup on staging today. 3/8 jobs hit timeouts at ~60s into generation.
devin: copying logs: 
```
[rank 2] kv_cache_warmup: missing_prefix=0.42s
[rank 5] kv_cache_warmup: missing_prefix=2.8s
allreduce: wait_ms median=1.9, p99=1200
rendezvous: heartbeat_miss=3
```
Looks asymmetric across ranks.
akshay: p99 allreduce 1200ms is wild — could be a comm/compute overlap collapse. Which kernel was selected on rank 5?
sylvia: profiler snapshot attached (summarized): continuous-batching fell to batch_size 1 on ranks 4/5; kernel_selector chose "matmul_fused_v2" for short seq on some ranks and "matmul_generic" on others.
maria: that's the suspicion: different kernel choices + uneven kv warmup causing some ranks to stall inside kv eviction path, then allreduce waits pile up.
devin: repro steps I ran: multi-node 8xA100, TP=4, pipeline microbatch=2, sequence skew by client injection. Repro seed attached. Can push a trace: 
```
# perf counters (rank5)
cuda_kernel_time: 1.2s
tensor_copy_wait: 0.6s
allreduce_wait: 1.1s
```
rank2 had kernel_time 0.4s.
akshay: So rank5 slower kernels + extra KV cache misses => longer compute -> missed progress heartbeats -> rendezvous times out on driver. Any RTT spikes on the NIC?
rui: NIC pings were stable, jitter < 100us. Network not root cause.
perf-bot: Automated perf diff: 
- change in batching heuristic at commit 0x7f1b increased variance in batch_size under skewed seqs (+0.18 var)
- kernel_selector commit 0x8a3b introduced an early exit to favor smaller memory footprints on ranks with low free_mem.
These two correlate with incident timestamps.
sylvia: idea: enforce deterministic kernel selection across ranks for the same model/seq_len bucket during rendezvous, at least for the first N steps to avoid asymmetry. Also warmup KV sync to ensure prefix caches are consistent.
maria: agree. short-term mitigation: bump rendezvous heartbeat and tolerate 5 missed heartbeats, and add a guard to fallback to a compatible kernel if allreduce_wait p99 > 300ms.
devin: can we get a lightweight patch: (1) kv sync barrier at start of generation, (2) add kernel selector override env REDWOOD_FORCE_KERNEL=matmul_fused_v2, (3) expose metric allreduce_wait_ms per-rank to console? I'll open a PR.
akshay: Also we should adjust batching heuristic: prefer stable batch_size for first 50 steps or until KV warmup complete. That reduces cross-rank imbalance.
rui: I'll run a canary with these toggles; ETA ~30m.
oncall-bot: Deploy started: canary/kv-resync-override on staging (build 2026-03-18_09:12).
perf-bot: After canary results: 30 runs, no timeouts; allreduce p99 dropped to 80ms; batch variance reduced 0.12; kernel choice consistent across ranks.
sylvia: nice. Follow-ups: 
- make KV-resync opt-in default for multi-node until kernel_selector change is reverted.
- add test that simulates seq-length skew for ci-perf to catch this.
- evaluate kernel_selector fallback policy instead of full revert.
maria: filed follow-up tasks in #eng-runtime sprint board. Thanks for fast triage. :tada:
devin: saved profiler snapshots to gcs://redwood-perf/1971234567/ for deeper analysis.
akshay: long term: revamp kernel scoring to include cross-rank performance signals (penalize kernels that increase inter-rank variance).
rui: re-running the multi-node stress now; will post final pass.
maria: closing thread once rui confirms stable for 6h. Thanks everyone.
